Judgment:
1.

The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954
(Pfa Act), alleging that the accused has violated the provisions of the Pfa Act and Rules.

The
acc

used Mahender Kumar is stated to be the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s. Samrat General Store,
from where the food article, that is, 'Arhar Dal' was lifted for sampling.

2. As per the complaint, on 14.08.2008, the food officials consisting of Food Inspector (FI)
Dharamvir Singh and Field Assistant (FA) Subedar Mishra under the supervision of Local Health Authority (LHA)/SDM Sh. Yogesh Partap reached along with their staff at the premises of M/s.
Samrat General Store at Shop No. 3, Shiv Mandir, Wazirabad, Delhi- 110054, where the accused was found conducting the business of various food articles, which were lying stored for sale for human consumption.

The FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of Dal Arhar from the vendor lying in open wooden box (ready for sale) bearing no label declaration, to which he had agreed.
The sample was then lifted as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules.
Each sample was separately packed, fastened, marked and sealed and necessary documents were prepared at the spot, including the Notice as per Form-VI, panchnama, etc.
The price of sample was paid to the vendor.
The vendor also failed to disclose the name of the supplier of such commodity.
Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample was sent to the Public Analyst (PA) in intact condition and the other two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA.

Vide report dated 04.09.2008, the PA found the sample to be adulterated on the ground that it was coloured with In Re vs Mahender Singh on 18 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111866397/
1 synthetic colouring matter 'Tartrazine'.

sentences.text: Upon receipt of report, the SDM/LHA ordered investigation which was carried out by the FI.
After completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA.

The complaint was then filed in the court by FI on 19.03.2009 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(a), (j) and (m) of PFA Act as well as Rules 23 and 29 of PFA Rules, as punishable section 7/16(1A) of PFA Act, and also violation of section 14A of the PFA Act as punishable under section 16(1C) of the Act.
3. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 13.09.2009.
The presence of the accused could be secured only 10.05.2010.

The matter was then listed for pre- charge evidence,
wherein the complainant examined PW-1 FI D. V. Singh.

On the basis of his deposition, charge was framed against the accused on 04.08.2012 for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1A) PFA Act, being violation of section 2(ia)(a), (j) and (m) of PFA Act, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

At the trial, the witness already examined in pre-charge stage was recalled for further cross-examination in post-charge stage and additionally, the prosecution examined PW-2 Sh. Yogesh Partap (SDM/LHA) and PW-3 FA S. Mishra in post-charge stage.

4. At the trial, PW-1, PW-2 and PW-3 who were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings, deposed about the proceedings conducted by them on 14.08.2008 and narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity,
expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of 1500 gms of Dal Arhar (ready for sale), mixing it using a clean and dry jhaba, separately sealing, packing and marking the samples, and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses.

They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex. PW-1/A, Notice as per Form-VI Ex. PW-1/B,
Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C and Raid Report Ex. PW-1/D. On the next working day that is 16.08.2008,
one counterpart of sample along with Memo as per Form-VII were sent to PA for analysis vide PA Receipt Ex. PW-1/E and remaining two counterparts with copy of Memos were deposited with LHA/SDM vide receipt Ex. PW-1/F.
PA report Ex. PW-1/G was received and upon direction of SDM/LHA, further investigation was carried out by PW-1 who sent letter Ex. PW-1/H to the vendor accused which remained unserved.
Letter Ex. PW-1/I was also sent to VAT office which was replied.
Thereafter, sanction Ex. PW-1/J was taken from the Director PFA and after completion of the investigation, complaint Ex. PW-1/K was filed in the court.
After this, intimation letter Ex. PW-1/L with copy of PA report was sent to the accused through registered post which did not return undelivered.
These witnesses were duly cross-examined by Ld. Defence Counsel wherein they denied that the jhaba or bottles were not clean and dry or that some yellow colour was sticking to them.
5. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC was recorded on 06.01.2016 wherein he denied the allegations and pleaded innocence.
He claimed that he was not present at the spot and that he came later on.
He stated that no efforts were made to join public witnesses and that no payment was made to him as price of the commodity.
He questioned the correctness of PA report and stated that no adulteration was made by him.
He stated that intimation letter was never served upon him.
He chose not to lead evidence in defence.

sentences.text: It is in these circumstances, Ld. SPP for the complainant has argued that the complainant has been able to establish its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt, on the ground that the accused has not been able to rebut the findings in the PA report dated 04.09.2008.
It is pointed out that the accused has failed to exercise his right under section 13(2) PFA Act and failed to get the sample analysed from Central Food Laboratory (CFL).
It is submitted that all the witnesses have supported its case and no major contradiction can be seen in their testimony.

7. On the other hand, Ld. Defence Counsel has contended that sample proceedings were not conducted properly and there is nothing to show that the jhaba or bottles used by the food officials were clean and dry.
It is claimed that the sample was not properly homogenized and also that no public witness was joined as required.

It is strongly contended that the intimation letter was never received by the accused, pointing out that postal receipt to establish such sending of letters has never been produced on record, nor any AD card or proof of service is there.
It is thus argued that the accused was prevented from exercising his right under section 13(2) of the PFA Act for getting the sample analysed through CFL.
8. I have heard the arguments advanced on behalf of both the sides and have carefully perused the material on record.

9. In a criminal trial, it is well settled that the burden to establish guilt of an accused beyond reasonable doubt is only upon the prosecution / complainant and this burden cannot be shifted to the accused.

The prosecution has to stand on its own legs to establish its case by leading positive,
cogent and trustworthy evidence.

10. There is no dispute to the settled legal proposition that once a prosecution has been initiated by the Complainant under PFA Act after receipt of the PA report by the LHA, it is the bounden duty of the LHA to send a copy of the PA report along with an intimation letter to the accused.
This is to enable the accused to exercise his right under section 13(2) of PFA Act which gives him an opportunity to get the counterpart of the lifted sample analysed through CFL.
Such a right has been recognized as a valuable and sacrosanct right and if this right has been frustrated by any act of the complainant, the benefit would always go in favour of the accused.

Reliance can be placed on the precedents titled as Rameshwar Dayal v. State of UP [1996 (2) PFA Cases 197 (SC)] and MCD v.
Ghisa Ram [AIR 1967 SC 970], which have been followed in a number of subsequent judgements.

entities.text: Rameshwar Dayal v. State of UP [1996 (2) PFA Cases 197 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. In the present case, it is claimed by the complainant that the intimation letter Ex. PW-1/L along with copy of PA report was sent to the accused through registered post.
Copy of the postal receipt Mark-X was placed on record by PW-1.
It is pertinent to mention that the examination in chief of PW-1 had been deferred on 08.02.2011 at the request of Ld. SPP as the witness had not brought the original postal receipt.
But when he stepped into the witness box again on 26.08.2011, he failed to bring the original record when he was further examined and cross-examined.
Two witnesses were examined thereafter but no record of postal receipts was proved by them.

Thus, what all remains on record is a photocopy of postal receipt Mark-X.
In Re vs Mahender Singh on 18 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111866397/
3 12.

entities.text: Re vs Mahender Singh on 18 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Such photocopy of a document is neither primary nor secondary evidence.
There is nothing to show that this copy had ever been compared with the original.
Original receipt was never produced on record by the witness despite his examination-in-chief having been deferred on this ground.
There is nothing to show that the original receipt has been lost or destroyed.
Thus, this photocopy is no evidence at all in the eyes of law.
13. In the absence of a postal receipt, it can not be established that the intimation letter with PA report were ever sent to the accused or were delivered to him.
This burden was only on the prosecution.
This is particularly when the PW-1 FI deposed that even during investigation, letter was sent to the accused but it had returned undelivered.
Even the summons of the court remained unexecuted for a number of times at this address.
On few occasions, the court had also observed that there was manipulation in the addresses mentioned on the summons.
In such position, it was all the more necessary for the prosecution to have produced on record the original receipt as well as the proof of service of intimation letter.
But the failure of the witnesses to produce the record despite requisition would lead the court to draw an adverse inference against the prosecution.
14. At this stage, the court is not oblivious of the fact that the accused has never taken such a defence at the trial.
He never put even a single suggestion to any PW that he never received the intimation letter with copy of PA report.
No such defence was put even to PW-1 despite his failure to produce the original record.
It was only when the evidence was over that the accused for the first time state in his statement under section 313 CrPC that he never received the intimation letter.

Record also shows that when the accused was evading service or court process and also warrants of arrest,
application was moved on his behalf for cancellation of NBWs which was dismissed due to his non-appearance.

At that time, he had also moved an application under section 13(2) PFA Act for exercising the right to get the sample analysed through CFL, stating that he had received the intimation letter and PA report.
But the date on which he received the same was left blank.
A bare perusal of the said application shows that it was nothing but a stereotype format in which the name and details of the accused were filled in hand.
In any case, there is no order of the court on this application.
There is no ordersheet in file or endorsement even on the application showing as to when this application was filed and when it was ordered to be placed on record.
There is no order of taking such application on record, or the accused pressing it, or the court considering or disposing it.
In such position, not much value can be attached to the averments contained in this application.
15. As stated earlier, it was the prime burden of the prosecution to have produced the material to discharge its initial burden.
Even the presumption of service under section 27 of the General Clause Act would come into effect only after this initial burden is discharged.
The material on record is not sufficient to show that intimation letter with PA report was sent to or served upon the accused.
Thus, the possibility of his right under section 13(2) PFA Act to have been frustrated, cannot be ruled out.
The accused is entitled to be given benefit of doubt on this count.
As such, there is no occasion for this court to go into the other issues as to manner of taking sample or non joining of public witnesses or correctness of PA report.
16. In view of the above discussion, the accused is acquitted of the charges.
However, his bail bond shall remain in force for the next six months in terms of section 437-A, CrPC.
